intro: Glaziers coordinate with crews, handle heavy materials carefully and work to tight measurements. The closest of the 25 careers below is Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters, with an 82% match, while Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic are 78% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $63,870, or 12% more.
why_it_works: Installing glass means measuring openings precisely, lifting and setting large panes safely and sealing them against weather. O*NET rates coordination and time management at 3 out of 5 for glaziers. Metal fabrication, rigging and layout work use the same mix of precision and physical work. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are quality checks and equipment maintenance.
tips: Power-line work is the best-paid close option: installers earn $95,320, which is 67% more.
Riggers earn $62,640, or 10% more, and use your skill moving heavy, fragile loads.
A welding certificate opens metal fabrication and many construction jobs.

faq.q: What jobs can former glaziers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters (82%), helpers for brick, stone and tile setters (78%) and metal and plastic layout workers (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Welders are 75% matched and earn $53,750, which is 6% less than the $57,080 glazier median.

faq.q: Which careers for glaziers pay more?
faq.a: 7 of the 25 matches pay more. Power-line installers earn $95,320 (67% more), layout workers $63,870 (12% more) and Riggers $62,640 (10% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Line work usually starts with a paid apprenticeship through a utility.

faq.q: Do glaziers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than glaziers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 77% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so certificates matter more than degrees.

The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, equipment maintenance, equipment selection and repairing. Complex problem solving already rates 2.88 out of 5 for glaziers in O*NET, so maintaining tools and machines is the main step toward better-paid trades.
